links.outcome: Specialized RAG LLM score versus neurosurgeons on VNS knowledge questionnaire
links.effect: AI scored 0.75, exceeding the highest individual clinician score (0.68; median 0.50), p < 0.001. AI better on anatomical/technical items; clinicians better on practical judgment.
links.quote: The AI achieved a score of 0.75, exceeding the highest individual clinician score (0.68; median: 0.50), with statistical significance (p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Hallucinations and precision of RAG-grounded LLM answers using curated VNS publication knowledge base
links.effect: Grounded in 125 curated VNS publications; perfect precision and specificity with no hallucinations detected.
links.quote: Confusion matrices revealed higher true correct and true incorrect rates for AI, demonstrating perfect precision and specificity scores with no hallucinations detected.

screen.reason: The study evaluated an LLM with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) against neurosurgeons on a multiple-choice knowledge assessment on vagus nerve stimulation, comparing baseline AI performance to clinicians rather than testing an organizational deployment safeguard or practice intervention.
